```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE)
library(nowcastNHSN)
gam_available <- requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("gratia", quietly = TRUE) &&
  utils::packageVersion("mgcv") >= "1.9-5" &&
  utils::packageVersion("gratia") >= "0.11.2"
```

## Introduction

In this vignette, we demonstrate swapping from the default baseline nowcasting method to the generalised additive model (GAM) nowcasting method.
Choosing a different nowcasting method is done by providing the corresponding configuration object to `nowcast()`.
Baseline and GAM methods use the same weekly reporting triangles and return `baselinenowcast_df` draws, so
the same summary and output functions work with either method.

GAM support uses the optional packages `mgcv` (at least 1.9-5) and `gratia`
(at least 0.11.2). These versions require R 4.4 or later. Baseline nowcasting
does not require these optional packages.

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("mgcv", "gratia"))
```

## Fetch NHSN reporting data

This example uses NHSN COVID-19 hospital admissions for California and New York
from the COVID-19 Forecast Hub, using the same package data source as the
[hub-data vignette](hubdata-source.html). We use the same period as the
[getting-started vignette](getting-started.html): reference weeks from
December 14, 2024 through July 5, 2025 (epiweeks 202450--202527), with reports
through July 26, 2025 (epiweek 202530). We nowcast as of July 5 and compare
the predictions with the counts available three weeks later. Only reports
available at the nowcast date enter the models; later reports are retained
for comparison.

```{r create-source}
source <- hub_data_source(
  hub_name = "covid19-forecast-hub",
  target = "wk inc covid hosp"
)
reference_start <- as.Date("2024-12-14")
cutoff <- as.Date("2025-07-05")
evaluation_date <- as.Date("2025-07-26")
```

Use `fetch_reporting_data()` to retrieve the cumulative reports.
Fetching live hub data requires the optional `hubData` and `arrow` packages.

```{r fetch-data, eval=FALSE}
reports <- fetch_reporting_data(
  source = source,
  reference_dates = seq(reference_start, cutoff, by = "week"),
  report_dates = seq(reference_start, evaluation_date, by = "week"),
  locations = c("ca", "ny"),
  dedup = "latest"
)
```

The built vignette uses the saved reporting-data snapshot shared with the
hub-data vignette, so its examples run without accessing the hub on each build.

```{r cached-data, include=FALSE}
reports <- readRDS("hubdata-source/reporting_data.rds")
```

## Prepare reporting triangles

The GAM nowcasting framework can pool information across locations to potentially improve predictions for locations with sparse data.
We set this up using the `strata` argument in `as_reporting_triangles()`, which creates a list of reporting triangle objects.
The source returns cumulative counts with Saturday reference and report dates.
Reporting delay is the number of weeks between `reference_date` and `report_date`.
Keep each series' initial report when preparing the triangle so that its first
increment includes the initially reported admissions.

```{r prepare-triangles}
reports <- reports |>
  dplyr::filter(
    reference_date >= reference_start, reference_date <= cutoff,
    report_date >= reference_start, report_date <= evaluation_date
  )
reports_at_cutoff <- reports |>
  dplyr::filter(report_date <= cutoff)

triangles <- as_reporting_triangles(
  reports_at_cutoff, strata = "location", nowcast_date = cutoff
)
triangles[c("location", "report_date")]
```

The collection stores one triangle and its effective observation date per
location. If a location has not reported at the requested vintage, its latest
available report is used. Advancing the requested vintage without new data
does not create additional observed reporting intervals.

For already incremental data, use `cumulative = FALSE`. Missing cumulative
snapshots are not filled before differencing: an increase between available
snapshots belongs to the later report. Observable gaps in the incremental
triangle are then filled with zero; future cells remain missing.

If triangles are already constructed, use
`reporting_triangles(triangles, keys, report_dates)`. The keys are a data frame
with one unique row per triangle, and observation dates must be supplied before
truncation can discard information about the latest report.

## Choose a GAM model

Both GAM presets model incremental reports with a negative-binomial distribution
and a log link.
A smooth reference-time term represents changing true admission levels over time.
Time and reporting-delay effects are additive on the log scale, so each fitted
series has a reporting-delay profile assumed to be stable over the training window.

- **GAM-Smooth** (`gam_smooth`) uses a smooth curve over reporting delays.
  Neighbouring delays share information, assuming the reporting-delay profile varies
  smoothly. The curve is not constrained to decrease with delay.
- **GAM-RE** (`gam_re`) estimates a separate random effect for each reporting delay,
  shrinking those effects towards a common mean. It allows abrupt differences
  between delays without assuming neighbouring delays have similar effects.

Both GAM presets fit the observed cells retained within the training window
(`training_weeks = 10` by default), including partially reported recent weeks.
Their uncertainty comes from coefficient draws and count sampling, with no
separate calibration subset.
This contrasts with the baseline method, which allocates historical data between estimating reporting delays for
point nowcasts and calibrating uncertainty from retrospective nowcast errors,
controlled by `scale_factor` and `prop_delay`.

By default, each series is fitted independently. Sharing information across
locations requires an explicit pooled model, as illustrated below.

```{r baseline}
draws <- 500L
set.seed(1)
baseline <- nowcast(triangles, nowcast_config(draws = draws))
head(summarize_nowcast(baseline))
```

```{r gam-models, eval=gam_available}
set.seed(1)
smooth <- nowcast(triangles, gam_nowcast_config("gam_smooth", draws = draws))
set.seed(1)
random_effect <- nowcast(triangles, gam_nowcast_config("gam_re", draws = draws))
head(summarize_nowcast(smooth))
```

Both GAM presets use a smooth reference-time term. GAM-Smooth adds a smooth
delay term, while GAM-RE uses a random-effect delay term. Defaults are a maximum
delay of seven weeks (including delay seven), a ten-week training window, and
1,000 draws. The training window is strictly later than the effective report
date minus ten weeks. Older reference dates remain in the returned output.

### Compare recent nowcasts

The plot shows the last seven reference weeks, comparing the incomplete data
available at the cutoff, the nowcasts, and the eventual data. Here, "eventual"
means the latest counts available by July 26, 2025, using the same comparison
date as the getting-started example. The newest plotted reference week has
four weeks of follow-up by that date, so these counts can still be revised.

As in the [getting-started vignette](getting-started.html), we join both sets of
reported counts to the nowcast summaries. We use 500 draws for the plotted
comparisons and fewer draws for the other API examples.

```{r plot-nowcasts, eval=gam_available, fig.width=8, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Baseline and GAM nowcasts using data available on July 5, 2025, compared with eventual counts available by July 26, 2025. Panels separate the models and states; blue bands show 90% prediction intervals.", class.source='fold-hide'}
library(ggplot2)

recent_start <- cutoff - 7 * 7
at_nowcast_time <- reports_at_cutoff |>
  dplyr::filter(reference_date >= recent_start, reference_date < cutoff) |>
  dplyr::group_by(location, reference_date) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(report_date, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(reference_date, location, at_nowcast = count)

eventual_counts <- reports |>
  dplyr::filter(
    report_date <= evaluation_date,
    reference_date >= recent_start, reference_date < cutoff
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(location, reference_date) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(report_date, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(reference_date, location, eventual = count)

comparison_counts <- at_nowcast_time |>
  dplyr::left_join(eventual_counts, by = c("location", "reference_date"))

model_draws <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  Baseline = baseline,
  `GAM-Smooth` = smooth,
  `GAM-RE` = random_effect,
  .id = "model"
)
model_intervals <- summarize_nowcast(model_draws, quantiles = c(.05, .5, .95)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = output_type_id, values_from = value, names_prefix = "q"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(reference_date >= recent_start, reference_date < cutoff) |>
  dplyr::left_join(comparison_counts, by = c("location", "reference_date")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = factor(model, levels = c("Baseline", "GAM-Smooth", "GAM-RE")))

count_colours <- c(
  `At Nowcast Time` = "#E41A1C", `Nowcast (Median)` = "#377EB8",
  `Eventual Data` = "#4DAF4A"
)
nowcast_plot <- ggplot(model_intervals, aes(x = reference_date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q0.05, ymax = q0.95, fill = "90% Prediction Interval"), alpha = .3) +
  geom_point(aes(y = at_nowcast, colour = "At Nowcast Time"), size = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = at_nowcast, colour = "At Nowcast Time"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = q0.5, colour = "Nowcast (Median)"), size = 2, shape = 17) +
  geom_line(aes(y = q0.5, colour = "Nowcast (Median)"), linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(y = eventual, colour = "Eventual Data"), size = 2, shape = 15) +
  geom_line(aes(y = eventual, colour = "Eventual Data"), linewidth = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(vars(location, model), scales = "free_y", ncol = 3,
             labeller = labeller(location = c(ca = "California", ny = "New York"))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = count_colours, breaks = names(count_colours)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`90% Prediction Interval` = "#377EB8")) +
  scale_x_date(breaks = seq(recent_start, cutoff - 7, by = "2 weeks"), date_labels = "%b %d") +
  labs(
    title = "GAM and baseline nowcasts",
    subtitle = "Nowcast: July 5, 2025 | eventual data: July 26, 2025",
    x = "Reference Date (Week Ending)", y = "Hospital Admissions",
    colour = "Count Type", fill = NULL
  ) +
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(
      shape = c(16, 17, 15), linetype = c("solid", "dashed", "dotted")
    )),
    fill = guide_legend(order = 2)
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical"
  )
nowcast_plot
```

The colours and symbols have the same meaning in every panel:

- **At Nowcast Time** (red circles): the counts available on July 5.
- **Nowcast (Median)** (blue triangles): the estimated counts after reporting
  delays, with a shaded 90% prediction interval.
- **Eventual Data** (green squares): the counts available by July 26.

Single triangles also work, with an explicit effective observation date:

```{r single-triangle, eval=gam_available}
single <- nowcast(
  triangles$triangle[[1]],
  gam_nowcast_config(draws = 25),
  nowcast_date = triangles$report_date[1]
)
```

The existing `run_state_nowcasts` runner function accepts either configuration and continues fitting
locations independently:

```{r runners, eval=gam_available}
mixed <- run_state_nowcasts(
  reports_at_cutoff,
  nowcast_config(draws = 25),
  location_configs = list(ny = gam_nowcast_config(draws = 25))
)
attr(mixed, "failed_locations")
```

Run different signals separately through these runners. Use a keyed collection
with `strata = c("location", "signal")` to retain multiple signals in the
triangle interface. Summaries retain each key; different models should likewise
be summarized separately unless their combined data explicitly include a
model identifier.

## Sampling approaches

The default `sampling = "delay"` samples the GAM's fitted means jointly, then
normalizes them over delays to obtain a reporting-completeness probability `p`
for each series, reference date, and draw. The final count is
`observed + rnbinom(size = observed, prob = p)`.

With `sampling = "posterior"`, the model samples future incremental counts
from the GAM's posterior predictive distribution and adds them to observed
counts. Both approaches use joint Metropolis-Hastings coefficient draws within
each fitted model.

```{r posterior, eval=gam_available}
posterior <- nowcast(
  triangles, gam_nowcast_config(sampling = "posterior", draws = 25)
)
```

Delay sampling produces zero when the observed total is zero. Posterior
sampling may produce additional reports for such a series when a pooled fit
has positive training observations. An entirely zero fitting group returns
zeros without fitting a GAM.

## Pool fitting and aggregate outputs separately

`fit_strata = NULL` fits each series independently. A subset of keys fits one
model for each combination of those keys; `character(0)` pools all series.
Stratum effects are not added automatically, so specify them in a formula
when needed.

Two states are enough to demonstrate fitting a shared delay curve. Here we
allow California and New York to have different admission levels and time
trends, while sharing the smooth effect of reporting delay. The formula uses
a fixed `location` effect and
[factor-by time smooths](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/mgcv/html/gam.models.html),
without estimating a state random-effect variance from two locations.

This is an illustration of the grouping interface. Whether the states have
sufficiently similar reporting delays for this assumption to improve nowcasts
would need retrospective evaluation across more vintages and locations.

```{r pooled-fit, eval=gam_available}
pooled_config <- gam_nowcast_config(
  formula = ~ location + s(origin, by = location, k = 3, bs = "cr") +
    s(lag, k = 3, bs = "cr"),
  fit_strata = character(0),
  draws = draws
)
set.seed(2)
pooled <- nowcast(triangles, pooled_config)
set.seed(2)
total <- nowcast(triangles, pooled_config, output_strata = character(0))
head(summarize_nowcast(total))
```

By default, each series remains separate in the output. `output_strata` names the keys to retain when summing final draws; `character(0)` sums all series.
Contributors must have matching reference-date coverage. Within a pooled fit, draw IDs retain shared coefficient uncertainty. Separately fitted groups contribute independent draws.
The same output aggregation works for baseline nowcasts.

### Compare independent and shared-delay fits

The next plot compares the independent GAM-Smooth fits above with this pooled
model, using the same data-at-cutoff and eventual-data comparison. Its bottom
row shows the CA + NY total, formed by summing each draw
before computing quantiles.

```{r plot-pooling, eval=gam_available, fig.width=8, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Independent and shared-delay GAM nowcasts at July 5, 2025, including their CA + NY totals, compared with eventual counts available by July 26, 2025. Red circles show data at the cutoff, blue triangles and bands show nowcasts and 90% prediction intervals, and green squares show eventual data.", class.source='fold-hide'}
independent_total <- smooth |>
  dplyr::group_by(reference_date, draw) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    pred_count = sum(pred_count), nowcast = any(nowcast),
    output_type = "samples", .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(location = "ca_ny")

pooling_draws <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  `Independent fits` = dplyr::bind_rows(smooth, independent_total),
  `Shared delay` = dplyr::bind_rows(pooled, dplyr::mutate(total, location = "ca_ny")),
  .id = "fit"
)
pooling_intervals <- summarize_nowcast(pooling_draws, quantiles = c(.05, .5, .95)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = output_type_id, values_from = value, names_prefix = "q"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(reference_date >= recent_start, reference_date < cutoff)

reported_total <- comparison_counts |>
  dplyr::group_by(reference_date) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    at_nowcast = sum(at_nowcast), eventual = sum(eventual), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(location = "ca_ny")
pooling_counts <- dplyr::bind_rows(comparison_counts, reported_total)
pooling_intervals <- pooling_intervals |>
  dplyr::left_join(pooling_counts, by = c("location", "reference_date")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(location = factor(location, levels = c("ca", "ny", "ca_ny")))

pooling_plot <- ggplot(pooling_intervals, aes(x = reference_date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q0.05, ymax = q0.95, fill = "90% Prediction Interval"), alpha = .3) +
  geom_point(aes(y = at_nowcast, colour = "At Nowcast Time"), size = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = at_nowcast, colour = "At Nowcast Time"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = q0.5, colour = "Nowcast (Median)"), size = 2, shape = 17) +
  geom_line(aes(y = q0.5, colour = "Nowcast (Median)"), linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(y = eventual, colour = "Eventual Data"), size = 2, shape = 15) +
  geom_line(aes(y = eventual, colour = "Eventual Data"), linewidth = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(vars(location, fit), scales = "free_y", ncol = 2,
             labeller = labeller(location = c(ca = "California", ny = "New York", ca_ny = "CA + NY"))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = count_colours, breaks = names(count_colours)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`90% Prediction Interval` = "#377EB8")) +
  scale_x_date(breaks = seq(recent_start, cutoff - 7, by = "2 weeks"), date_labels = "%b %d") +
  labs(
    title = "Independent versus shared-delay GAMs",
    subtitle = "Nowcast: July 5, 2025 | eventual data: July 26, 2025",
    x = "Reference Date (Week Ending)", y = "Hospital Admissions",
    colour = "Count Type", fill = NULL
  ) +
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(
      shape = c(16, 17, 15), linetype = c("solid", "dashed", "dotted")
    )),
    fill = guide_legend(order = 2)
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical"
  )
pooling_plot
```

Formula predictors include `origin` (days since the earliest training reference
date plus one), `lag`, their factor versions `origin_f` and `lag_f`, and the
series keys. The predictor `lag` encodes reporting delay as `7 * delay + 1`,
where `delay` is measured in weeks. Additional predictors are `delay`, `reference_date`,
`report_date`, `season`, `origin_s`, `dow_reference_date`, and
`dow_reference_date_factor`. Seasons start October 1; `origin_s` uses each
season's earliest training reference date. Keys are factors during fitting;
outputs preserve their original types. Prediction reuses training coordinates
and factor levels.

Preset and custom formulas are fitted as specified, without automatically
changing terms when data are sparse. If fitting fails, the original `mgcv`
error is preserved alongside the affected series or fitting group.

## Fixed delay offsets

`delay_prior` supplies positive offsets for every delay in the configured
horizon. Optional key columns allow offsets to vary across series. The offsets
enter the GAM on the log scale in both training and prediction. They are fixed
predictors, not a distribution of uncertain prior parameters.

```{r delay-offset, eval=gam_available}
offsets <- data.frame(delay = 0:7, offset = exp(-(0:7) / 2))
with_offsets <- nowcast(
  triangles, gam_nowcast_config(delay_prior = offsets, draws = 25)
)
```

Without offsets, fitting and prediction stop at the largest delay with positive
training counts in the fitting group. With offsets, the entire configured
horizon is retained. In both cases, observed totals come from the full
configured triangle.

## Revisions, output, and failures

Negative increments are redistributed backward after maximum-delay truncation.
For example, increments `100, 20, -5` become `100, 15, 0`, preserving the observed
total of 115. Revisions outside the configured horizon have already been
excluded. The GAM estimates additional nonnegative reports and cannot predict
future downward revisions.

Every output contains `reference_date`, `pred_count`, `draw`, `output_type`,
`nowcast`, and retained series keys. Complete dates have repeated observed-count
draws. `nowcast` describes missing cells in the configured triangle; it can
remain `TRUE` for deterministic draws when fitted delay support ends earlier.
Aggregated rows are flagged if any contributor is incomplete.

`summarize_nowcast()` preserves all series keys. Parquet output also preserves
them, but the existing location-partitioned writer requires a `location` column.
A total with location aggregated away can still be summarized in memory.

Fit and sampling failures are errors with group context. A direct grouped
`nowcast()` call fails as a whole rather than returning partial totals. Location
runners retain their existing per-location failure handling. No convergence or
sampling error is silently replaced by zeros.
